text: Know the type of confidential information held by organisations
points: human resources: salaries and benefits, staff personal details
commercially sensitive information: client details, stakeholder details, intellectual property, sales numbers, contracts
access information: usernames, passwords, MFA details, PINs, access codes, passphrases, biometric data

text: Understand why information must be kept confidential by organisations
Understand the potential impact to an organisation of failing to maintain privacy and confidentiality
points: non-compliance with regulations: loss of licence to practise
financial loss: fines, refunds, loss of earnings/termination of contracts

text: Understand potential technical threats and their impacts on organisations and individuals, including prevention and mitigation methods
points: malicious hacking: hacktivists, nation states, organised crime, individuals; password cracking/brute force; cross-site scripting; SQL injection; buffer overflow
malware: viruses, worms, key loggers, ransomware, spyware, remote access trojans
social engineering: phishing, spear phishing, smishing, vishing, pharming, watering hole attacks, USB baiting

text: Understand potential technical vulnerabilities to systems and data
points: inadequate security processes: weak encryption, inadequate password policy, failure to use MFA
out-of-date components: hardware; software (lack of support, legacy compatibility, zero-day bugs); firmware

text: Understand potential human threats, including prevention and mitigation methods
points: human error: file properties, confirmation boxes, staff training
malicious employee: immediate removal from premises, suspend user accounts immediately
disguised criminal: accompany all visitors, check identification
poor cyber hygiene: lock unattended machines, do not write down passwords, poor password management

text: Understand potential physical vulnerabilities, including prevention and mitigation methods
points: lack of access control: entry control systems
poor access control: no tailgating, complex access codes, change codes regularly, monitor access areas, audit staff access
nature of location: shoulder surfing, environment, vandalism

text: Understand the potential impact to an organisation of threats and vulnerabilities
points: unauthorised access to restricted physical areas

text: Understand the purposes, processes, benefits and drawbacks of common threat mitigation techniques
points: security settings (hardware, software); anti-malware (function, actions); intrusion detection
user access policies; staff vetting; staff training; software-based access control
device hardening; backups (full, incremental, differential; safe storage); software updates; firmware/driver updates; air gaps
certification of APIs; VPNs; multi-factor authentication; password managers
port scanning; penetration testing (ethical and unethical hacking)

text: Understand the processes and procedures that assure internet security and the reasons why they are used
points: firewall configuration: inbound and outbound rules, traffic type rules, application rules, IP address rules
network segregation: virtual, physical, offline network

heading: 8.4 Interrelationship of components required for effective security

text: Understand how the relationships in the CIA triad interrelate
points: integrity: data not tampered with; supported by confidentiality
availability: data available and useful; supported by integrity

text: Understand the elements of the IAAA model, including techniques and their benefits and drawbacks
points: authentication: MFA, passwords and passphrases, biometrics
